hook.text: Neanderthal populations probably never exceeded 70,000. Homo sapiens may have outnumbered them ten to one.

buildup.text: Greater sapiens numbers meant more genetic diversity, more innovation, and faster recovery from disasters.

discovery.text: Even a small, steady reproductive advantage—one extra surviving child per generation—compounds over millennia.

twist.text: Neanderthals didn't need to be inferior. Being slightly outnumbered was enough to seal their fate.

climax.text: Demographic models show replacement could happen in just a few thousand years with tiny fitness differences.

punchline.text: They didn't lose a war. They lost a math problem.

quiz.question: Why were Neanderthal populations vulnerable to replacement?
options: Small population size meant even tiny disadvantages compounded
A plague wiped them out instantly
